extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting to Nature Catalysis, their institutional press offices, researchers and journalists covering Nature Portfolio content
extracted.subtask_description: Official press-release and embargo rules for articles submitted to Nature Catalysis (and Nature Portfolio journals), covering when and how authors, institutions and journalists may communicate about submitted, accepted, preprint or in-press material. Includes guidance on press releases, access for journalists, embargo timing, and conduct around preprints and conference presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discouragement of direct solicitation of media for submitted material
rubrics_metrics.description: We strongly discourage authors and potential authors from direct solicitation of media coverage of material they have submitted to Nature and the Nature Portfolio journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should avoid contacting media to solicit coverage while the manuscript is under consideration. See related guidance on communications between scientists for preprints and conference presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: When accepted contributions may be discussed with media
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted contributions can be discussed with the media only once the publication date has been confirmed and no more than a week before the publication date under our embargo conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion with media prior to this window is not permitted; coordination with the journal's embargo timetable is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production and distribution of press releases by the journal
rubrics_metrics.description: We produce and distribute press releases summarizing upcoming content to a list of registered journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The press office prepares and issues summaries of selected upcoming papers; these press releases may highlight particularly newsworthy items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalists' encouraged practices on reading and contacting authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists are encouraged to read the full version of any papers they wish to cover, and are given the names and contact details of corresponding authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should consult the full paper (not just the press release) and may contact corresponding authors; authors should be prepared to respond accurately and are encouraged to cooperate to ensure balanced coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance access for journalists to full text and supporting materials
rubrics_metrics.description: They receive access to the full text of papers about a week before publication on a password-protected website, together with other relevant material (for example, an accompanying News and Views article, and any extra images provided by the authors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access is controlled and intended to allow informed reporting based on the complete and final version of the paper; materials remain embargoed until the stated time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo of press release content and papers
rubrics_metrics.description: The content of the press release and papers is embargoed until the time and date clearly stated on the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All recipients must respect the embargo time/date; the press release explicitly states when information may be made public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlighting especially newsworthy papers on press release
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers that are deemed especially newsworthy are highlighted by a brief summary on the press release for that journal, written by the editors and the press office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such highlights may draw media attention; authors should expect possible contact from media during the embargo window and work with journalists to ensure accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors may arrange their own publicity but must adhere to embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors whose papers are scheduled for publication may also arrange their own publicity (for instance through their institutional press offices), but they must strictly adhere to our media embargo and are advised to coordinate their own publicity with our press office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate timing and messaging with the journal's press office to avoid premature release and inconsistent information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale: embargo serves fair and equal access and informed comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Our policy is to release information about our content in a way that provides fair and equal access to the media, allowing it to provide informed comment based on the complete and final version of the paper that is to be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embedding embargoed advance access enables journalists to prepare accurate coverage and obtain independent reactions; it benefits scientists, authors, journalists and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harm of premature release
rubrics_metrics.description: Premature release to the media denies journalists that confidence. It also removes journalists' ability to obtain informed reactions about the work from independent researchers in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and institutions should avoid disseminating results prematurely as this undermines the peer-review-backed context journalists rely on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for breaking embargoes
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists who break our embargoes have been removed from the press-release circulation list, and we shall continue to use this sanction when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breach of embargo may result in removal from future advance-access distributions; the journal enforces embargo compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprints and conference presentations do not constitute prior publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Portfolio journals do not wish to hinder communication among researchers. We support open communications between researchers whether on a recognised community preprint server or preprint commenting platforms, through discussions at research meetings or online collaborative sites such as wikis or the author's blog. Neither conference presentations nor posting on recognized preprint servers constitute prior publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posting on established preprint servers before or during submission is permitted and does not preempt submission; consult the journal's preprint policy pages for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to media about preprints or conference presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers may respond to requests from the media in response to a preprint or conference presentation, by providing explanation or clarification of the work, or information about its context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When responding, make clear the work has not yet undergone peer review, that findings are provisional and conclusions may change; such media engagement will not necessarily hinder editorial handling but may pre-empt later coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of peer-review and editorial process
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are expected to keep the details of the peer review and editorial process confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not disclose peer-review correspondence or confidential editorial steps when engaging with media or others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation for reporters covering preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: We also recommend that reporters who cover preprints clearly indicate that the study has not been peer reviewed and that the claims may change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should explicitly state the preprint status and provisional nature of findings when reporting on non-peer-reviewed work.
